Practical Spiritual Practices

Philosophy without practice is just intellectual entertainment. Sanatan Dharma is rooted in the laboratory of the self—discover the methodologies of awakening.

In the East, theology is secondary; realization is primary. Sanatan Dharma prescribes specific, replicable technologies to alter human consciousness. Depending on your temperament—intellectual, active, or emotional—there is a specific toolkit designed for you.

This is the concept of Sadhana (spiritual exertion or practice). A person engaged in Sadhana is a Sadhaka. Below you will find the dominant practices utilized by yogis and householders alike for thousands of years.

Meditation (Dhyana)

The systematic process of silencing the mind to experience the true nature of the self. From basic mindfulness to deep absorption (Samadhi).

Explore

Mantra Japa

The repetition of sacred sonic formulas (Mantras) to focus the mind, alter psychological patterns, and tune into divine frequencies. Using malas and sound.

Explore

Bhakti & Puja

The path of radical love. Through ritual worship (Puja), chanting (Kirtan), and surrender, the heart is purified and the ego is dissolved in devotion.

Explore

Hatha & Ashtanga Yoga

The physical and energetic disciplines (Asana, Pranayama) designed to purify the body's channels (Nadis) to safely handle higher states of consciousness.
